title: yt-dlp vs youtube-dl: What Changed and What to Do | HJ Video Downloader
description: An objective comparison of yt-dlp and youtube-dl across maintenance status, download speed, site coverage, licence and options, plus what to watch for when migrating existing scripts.
sub: How they relate, what actually differs, and three migration notes
tldr: yt-dlp is the actively maintained fork of youtube-dl. After youtube-dl's development slowed down, the community carried maintenance forward in yt-dlp, fixing broken extractors whenever platforms change, and adding concurrent fragmented downloads, richer metadata handling and finer format selection. New projects generally pick yt-dlp.

matrix.caption: yt-dlp and youtube-dl compared objectively
rows: Actively maintained, keeps up with platform changes
Historically broad, but new sites and token support lag
Concurrent fragmented downloads, better use of bandwidth

sections.heading: How the two are related
paragraphs: youtube-dl is the original open-source command line downloader with a huge list of supported sites. As its release cadence slowed, extractors broke on platforms that changed often, and the community forked maintenance into yt-dlp.
Both are released under the Unlicense (public domain) and their command styles are close, which is why migrating usually costs little. HJ Video Downloader runs on yt-dlp.

sections.heading: Five dimensions compared
paragraphs: Maintenance is the most practical difference: platforms rotate signatures several times a year, and only a fork that follows along still works today.
On transfer, yt-dlp supports concurrent fragments, friendlier to long videos and large files; youtube-dl is mostly single connection.
On selection, yt-dlp offers richer expressions so you can pin down a stream by resolution, codec and bitrate.
On metadata, yt-dlp exposes more options around subtitles, chapters and thumbnails — one reason this site can read subtitle tracks directly for AI summaries.

sections.heading: Migration notes
paragraphs: Most everyday flags (-f, -o, --no-playlist) behave the same, so swapping the command name is usually enough; a few names and defaults differ, so check the official docs.
Format expressions are richer: keep your old -f string until everything works, then refine it if you need to.
Newer releases require a recent Python — mind your runtime — and ffmpeg remains required for merging streams.

sections.heading: When youtube-dl still turns up
paragraphs: Long-lived environments that never upgrade tend to keep the old binary for stability, and some distribution repositories still ship youtube-dl.
For anything new, the usual advice is yt-dlp plus routine upgrades — which is why this project updates the core automatically at startup.

pick.answer: Use yt-dlp and put auto-updates in your startup routine
Swap the command name, get it green, then adopt the new expressions
Keep the old version and accept that some sites will drift out of support

conclusion: In one line: yt-dlp is youtube-dl's active successor, and it should be the default choice for almost every scenario.
